# Cleaning and Exploring the Data

```{r}
# Creating a filtered dataset, removing previously identified invalid responses
data <- read_excel("actual survey ver. 2.xlsx")
data2 <- data[-c(201, 231, 420, 457, 458), ]
```

```{r}
# Removing metadata columns
data2 <- data2 %>%
  select(-start_001, -end_001, -today_001, -pair_area, -pair_id, -enumerator, -q_code_num,
         -assigned_area, -confirmation, -`_id`, -`_uuid`, -`_submission_time`, 
         -`_validation_status`, -`_notes`, -`_status`, -`_submitted_by`, -`__version__`, 
         -`_tags`, -`meta/rootUuid`, -`_index`) 
        # 20 cols removed

# Removing empty columns (structural/formatting & instructional columns)
names(data2)[colSums(!is.na(data2)) == 0]       # 27 cols removed
data2 <- data2%>%
  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.)))) %>%
  select(-d1, -d2, -d3, -d4, -e2, -e3, -e5 )    # 7 cols removed

# Total of 54 cols removed
```

```{r}
# Checking data type of all remaining columns
cols_type <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(data2),
  Type = sapply(data2, function(x) class(x)[1]) # Take only the first class label
  )
View(cols_type)
```

```{r}
# Renaming variables for consistency (and conciseness)
data2 <- data2 %>%
  rename_with(~ gsub("-", "_", .)) %>%    # replacing dashes with underscores for the binary variables created by Kobo
  rename(
    e1_1       = e1_1_pr1,
    e1_2       = e1_2_ar1,
    c4_6_1_vb  = c4_6_1_text,
    c6_4_1_vb  = c6_4_1_text,   
    f1_1_vb    = f1_1_verbatim,
    f1_2_vb    = f1_2_verbatim,
    f2_vb      = f2_verbatim,
    f3_vb      = f3_1,          
    f4_vb      = f4_1,           
    g5_vb      = g5_verbatim
  )
head(data2)
```

```{r}
# Changing binary variable values to 1 and 0 instead of 1 and 2 (e.g. 1 - Oo, 0 - Hindi)
bin_cols <- c("a2", "c6_4", "c6_4_2", "f1", "g1")
data2 <- data2 %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(bin_cols), ~ case_when(
    . == 1 ~ 1,
    . == 2 ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_  # Handles any NAs or weird entries safely
  )))
```

```{r}
# Rounding street to 2 decimal places
data2<- data2 %>%
  mutate(street = round(as.numeric(street), 2))
```

```{r}
# Reformatting verbatim responses with multiple lines
data2 <- data2 %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), ~ str_replace_all(., "[\r\n]+", " ")))
# i did this because i saw a weird string in the value of one of the rows for c4_6_1_text when viewed in the console (caused by enumerators pressing Enter button to input the next line)
```

```{r}
# Checking eligibility based on age (still checking above 60 to capture outliers/value of "143")
flagged_age <- data2 %>%
  filter(a1 < 18 | a1 > 60 | is.na(1)) %>%
  select(username, q_code, a1)
View(flagged_age)
# Result: Two values flagged (value = 143, 98)

# Verified that the age of the respondent tagged with "143" is actually 51 and that the age of the respondent originally said to be 98 is 30
# Manipulating the dataset
data_screened <- data2 %>%
  mutate(a1 = case_when(
    q_code == "6305" ~ 51,
    q_code == "6409" ~ 30,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(a1) # Keep everything else as is
  ))

# Checking that age of q_code 6305 is now 51 and the age of q_code 6409 is now 30
data_screened %>% 
  filter(q_code == 6305 | q_code == 6409) %>% 
  select(q_code, a1)
```

```{r}
# Checking eligiblity based on commute criteria
# VERSION 3 (travel at least 2x a week, at least 7.5 mins each (since this will be doubled for a combined 15 min travel))
# Creating the 'Estimated Combined' columns (2x the one-way duration)
data_screened <- data_screened %>%
  mutate(
    c3_1_comb = replace_na(c3_1_trbho_dur, 0) * 2,
    c3_2_comb = replace_na(c3_2_sch_dur, 0)   * 2,
    c3_3_comb = replace_na(c3_3_hh_err_dur, 0) * 2,
    c3_4_comb = replace_na(c3_4_lib_dur, 0)    * 2,
    c3_5_comb = replace_na(c3_5_health_dur, 0) * 2,
    c3_6_comb = replace_na(c3_6_oth_dur, 0)    * 2
  )

# Counting frequencies for trips where the COMBINED duration is 15+
data_screened <- data_screened %>%
  mutate(
    v3_work   = ifelse(c3_1_comb >= 15, c3_1_trbho_byahe, 0),
    v3_school = ifelse(c3_2_comb >= 15, c3_2_sch_byahe,   0),
    v3_errand = ifelse(c3_3_comb >= 15, c3_3_hh_err_byahe, 0),
    v3_lib    = ifelse(c3_4_comb >= 15, c3_4_lib_byahe,    0),
    v3_health = ifelse(c3_5_comb >= 15, c3_5_health_byahe, 0),
    v3_other  = ifelse(c3_6_comb >= 15, c3_6_oth_byahe,    0)
  )

# Final sum and eligibility 
data_screened <- data_screened %>%
  mutate(
    v3_total_trips = v3_work + v3_school + v3_errand + v3_lib + v3_health + v3_other
  )
ineligible_commute <- data_screened %>%
  filter(v3_total_trips < 2) %>%
  select(username, q_code, v3_total_trips, contains("_comb"), contains("_byahe"))

View(ineligible_commute)

# 45 respondents ineligible based on commute criteria
```

```{r}
# Creating the 'clean' dataset and removing audit columns
data_clean <- data_screened %>%
  filter(v3_total_trips >= 2) %>%
  select(-starts_with("v3_"), -contains("_comb")) # Removing additional columns created in checking eligibility
# Check the final sample size (should be 629 if we started at 674)
nrow(data_clean)
```

```{r}
# Checking for outliers in no. of dependents
# Calculating the IQR and Fences for B3_count
Q1 <- quantile(data_clean$b3_count, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
Q3 <- quantile(data_clean$b3_count, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR_val <- IQR(data_clean$b3_count, na.rm = TRUE)

upper_fence <- Q3 + 1.5 * IQR_val
lower_fence <- Q1 - 1.5 * IQR_val

# Extracting the exact rows
b3_outlier_rows <- data_clean %>%
  filter(b3_count > upper_fence | b3_count < lower_fence) %>%
  select(q_code, b3_count, everything())

View(b3_outlier_rows)

# Flagged outliers: 20 dependents (2 respondents)
```

# Report

## Time Series of Response Submissions

```{r}
# Version 1
# Preparing the data (raw dataset)
deadline <- as.POSIXct("2026-05-07 23:59:59")

time_series<- data %>%
  # Filtering only for responses encoded up to the deadline
  filter(`_submission_time` <= deadline) %>%
  # Converting POSIXct to Date for daily grouping
  mutate(date_only = as.Date(`_submission_time`)) %>%
  # Counting responses per day
  group_by(date_only) %>%
  summarise(daily_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # Ensuring chronological order for cumulative sum
  arrange(date_only) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_responses = cumsum(daily_count))

# Visualization
ggplot(time_series, aes(x = date_only, y = cumulative_responses)) +
  # Shaded area for visual volume
  geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  # Main progress line
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  # Data points for each day
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 2) +
  
  annotate("label", 
           x = max(time_series$date_only), 
           y = max(time_series$cumulative_responses), 
           label = paste("Total Encoded:", max(time_series$cumulative_responses)),
           fill = "white", 
           fontface = "bold", 
           color = "darkblue",
           hjust = 1.1) + # Nudges the text box to the left so it won't cut off
  
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %d", 
               date_breaks = "3 days",
               expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.1))) + # Adds 20% extra space on the right
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Data Collection Progress (Original Dataset)",
    subtitle = "Cumulative submissions through Thursday, 11:59 PM",
    x = "Date of Encoding",
    y = "Total Number of Forms"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    # Allows the label to exist outside the panel if needed
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10) 
  )
```

```{r}
# Version 2
# Preparing the data
deadline <- as.POSIXct("2026-05-07 23:59:59")

time_series <- data %>%
  filter(`_submission_time` <= deadline) %>%
  mutate(date_only = as.Date(`_submission_time`)) %>%
  group_by(date_only) %>%
  summarise(daily_count = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(date_only) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_responses = cumsum(daily_count))

# 2. VISUALIZATION
ggplot(time_series, aes(x = date_only, y = cumulative_responses)) +
  # Area and line for the "growth" look
  geom_area(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "darkblue", size = 2.5) +
  
  # LABEL EVERY DAY: 
  geom_label(aes(label = cumulative_responses),
             vjust = -0.7,   # Sits slightly above the point
             hjust = 0.5,    # Centered horizontally on the point
             size = 3.5, 
             fontface = "bold",
             fill = "white",
             color = "darkblue",
             label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines")) +
  
  # Using breaks = time_series_og$date_only ensures every day shows up on the X-axis
  scale_x_date(breaks = time_series$date_only,
               date_labels = "%b %d", 
               expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.1))) + 
  
  # Ensurea the Y-axis has room for the labels at the top
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Data Collection Progress",
    subtitle = "Cumulative submissions from April 25 to May 7",
    x = "Date of Encoding",
    y = "Total Number of Forms"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5) # Keep dates horizontal
  )
```

## Other Graphs

```{r}
# No. of respondents per area

# Preparing data
area_counts <- data_clean %>%
  count(area) %>%      # Counting respondents per area
  arrange(desc(n))     # Sorting from highest to lowest

# Visualization
ggplot(area_counts, aes(x = reorder(area, -n), y = n, fill = area)) +
  # Creating the bars
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Adding the exact count on top of each bar
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 4) +
  
  # Using a distinct color palette for the 7 areas
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") + 
  
  # Ensuring the Y-axis has room for the labels at the top
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Total Respondents per Area",
    subtitle = paste("Total Sample Size: n =", sum(area_counts$n)),
    x = "Area Number",
    y = "Number of Respondents"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none", # Hiding legend since area names are on the X-axis
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, size = 10, vjust = 0.5), # Changing ngle to 45 if names are long
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() # Cleaning up the look
  )
```

```{r}
# Eligible vs. Ineligible Respondents
# Preparing the data
total_raw <- nrow(data2)
total_clean <- nrow(data_clean)
total_ineligible <- total_raw - total_clean

eligibility_data <- data.frame(
  Status = c("Eligible", "Ineligible"),
  Count = c(total_clean, total_ineligible)
)

# Visualization
ggplot(eligibility_data, aes(x = "", y = Count, fill = Status)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.5) +
  # One-line label with a smaller font size to fit inside the red bar
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Count, " (", round(Count/total_raw*100, 1), "%)")), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), 
            color = "white", 
            fontface = "bold",
            size = 2.8) + # Shrunk the size slightly so it stays inside
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Eligible" = "#2ecc71", "Ineligible" = "#e74c3c")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Final Sample Eligibility Summary",
    subtitle = paste("Total Encoded Forms:", total_raw),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Number of Respondents"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    # Keeping your original title/subtitle sizes
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), 
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
```
